newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes higher as soybeans/meal rally.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes higher as soybeans/meal rally.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher on a late rally in soybean and soymeal futures, traders said.
But corn found independent strength, especially in the new crop December, on forecasts for spring flooding in the U.S. Midwest which could lead to a shift away from corn acres into soybeans.
Traders said the expiration of the March CBOT grain and soy complex helped encourage renewed buying in all pits. March corn expired at 1201 CST Wednesday down 3-1/2 cents per bushel at $3.02-1/2.

Position squaring was noted before the release Thursday of USDA's weekly export sales report. Trade expectations for the government's net corn export sales tally were from 650,000 to 1,000,000 tonnes.

Deliveries Wednesday on the March were at 1.305 million bushels but Continental Grain stopped most of the corn. CBOT corn registrations late Wednesday increased another 325,000 bushels, 100,000 in Toledo and 225,000 in Chicago.
Corn closed 2-1/4 to 4-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with May up 2-1/4 at $3.03-1/4 and December 4-1/2 cents higher at $2.93.
Traders said ongoing talk China sold corn to Malaysia may have limited gains but much of the bearish impact of that scenario was factored into the market during Tuesday's session.

Traders in Kuala Lumpur Wednesday said Malaysia and Thailand are said to have bought up to 80,000 tonnes of Chinese and Argentine corn in the past two weeks. Indonesia may also be looking to pick up more corn from China, the traders said.

CBOT corn futures also may have taken note that Taiwan Sugar Corp Wednesday passed on a tender for a 10,000 tonne U.S. corn shipment. Also Taiwan's Members Feed Industry Group has moved to Friday a tender initially set for Thursday for up to 112,000 tonnes of U.S. or Argentine corn.
But USDA early Wednesday said U.S. exporters reported a sale of 103,632 tonnes of corn to Japan.
Technicians early Wednesday cited first support in the May at $2.99 and second support at $2.94-1/4. The session low for May was $2.99-1/4.
First resistance was at $3.03-3/4 and second resistance was at $3.08-1/2. The session high for the May was $3.03-1/2.
Chartists said the four- and 20-day moving averages for the May early Wednesday were giving off bullish signals.
The short term nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for the May closed at 56.5 percent. The market considers an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.

Iowa Grain bought four million bushels of December and Refco Inc bought 2.5 million bushels of July, traders said. Refco also sold one million bushels of May and December and Griffin Trading sold two million bushels of July and sold one million bushels of May, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 58,000 contracts, below the 73,195 traded Tuesday.
In corn options, LIT America bought 300 July $3.20 calls at 10-1/4 cents, Tenco Inc sold 1,000 July $2.80 calls at 26-1/2 cents and Smith Barney sold 500 May $3.30 calls at two cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 17,000 contracts, above the 12,475 traded Tuesday.
